A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hyper-Connections with the same authors, method, and principal experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training, downstream evaluations, ablations, and ImageNet generation and classification experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds training curves and analyses of learned connection weights.

M1.justification: The static and dynamic hyper-connection equations, initialization, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. New Algorithm 3 illustrates integration into the existing transformer procedure rather than introducing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dolma and OLMoE training coverage, language evaluation tasks, and ImageNet generation/classification tasks. Analyzing three existing ImageNet categories and extending training duration do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged, including Altup and ResiDual in Table 4 and the corresponding language and vision baselines. New Figure 15 supplies training curves for the existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 Figures 16–17 add extended-budget OLMo-1B comparisons, with training curves reaching approximately one trillion tokens rather than ending at 500B. This substantially extends the tested training horizon. The original benchmark protocols remain, although Section 4's statement that all experiments use 500B tokens is not reconciled with these plots.

E4.justification: v2 adds category-dependent DHC weight analysis, an investigation of why expansion rate n=1 fails, and longer-horizon expansion-rate comparisons. New ViT and comparator training curves also expose training dynamics. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained ablations and connection visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run performance uncertainty, or significance tests. Figure 3's median and percentile bands are retained. The new weight histograms describe learned weights rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: Existing language, MoE, and ImageNet benchmark scores remain unchanged. v2 adds substantial supplementary results: longer training-loss trajectories, category-dependent weight distributions, the observation that layer 17 lacks downstream connections at n=1, and parameter/FLOP entries in Tables 5, 7, and 8.

T1.justification: New Appendix B derives SHC/DHC parameter counts and analyzes computational and activation-memory scaling. The original residual-equivalence, unfolded-connection, and sequential-parallel derivations are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions. The introduction adds an explicit necessity claim for n>1, stating that n=1 retains the gradient/representation seesaw, thereby qualifying the scope of the proposed flexibility.

C2.justification: v2 explains n=1 failure through its inability to form the Λ-shaped connection pattern and possible gradient vanishing. It also proposes repeated dataset exposure as the reason for diminishing ViT training-loss gains. These are focused additions to otherwise retained interpretations.

D1.justification: Algorithm 3 newly documents attention/FFN integration, normalization, and dropout placement. Appendix B adds normalization-parameter conventions and resource accounting, including a suggested activation-recomputation strategy. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the existing implementation or training recipe.

R1.justification: v2 adds Korthikanti et al. (2022), Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models, to support its memory analysis. The remaining cited works and principal research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction receives localized explanatory rewriting, terminology and spelling receive small edits, and appendix sections are inserted and relettered. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redesigned to contrast residual and hyper-connections. v2 adds a transformer architecture diagram, diagnostic visualizations, training-curve figures, and two resource tables; Table 5 gains parameter/FLOP columns. Table captions also move above their tables, substantially expanding and revising the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added diagnostics, longer training curves, resource accounting, and transformer pseudocode improve assessment and implementation of the retained method. The net gain is limited by inconsistencies: Table 7's SHC×4 parameter count conflicts with the 768-parameter derivation, and the blanket 500B training description is not reconciled with Figures 16–17. These local problems temper the useful additions.
